questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fact: Two pump blood to the gills, one pumps it to the rest of the body.

questions.q: What is a group of crows called?
questions.fact: A group of owls is called a parliament.

questions.q: What color is a polar bear's skin?
questions.fact: Black skin soaks up heat. The fur isn't white either, it's see-through.

questions.q: Which of these animals can't jump?
questions.fact: An elephant always keeps at least one foot on the ground.

questions.q: Which animal has fingerprints like ours?
questions.fact: Koala prints are so close to human ones they're hard to tell apart.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.

questions.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: So the Sun you see is about 8 minutes old.

questions.q: Which planet has the most moons?
questions.fact: Saturn has well over 200 known moons.

questions.q: What is the hottest planet?
questions.fact: Its thick clouds trap heat, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

questions.q: On Venus, which one is longer?
questions.fact: One Venus day is about 243 Earth days. Its year is about 225.

questions.q: How many bones does an adult have?
questions.fact: Babies are born with around 300. Some fuse together as you grow.

questions.q: What is the largest organ in your body?
questions.fact: Your skin is constantly shedding and replacing itself.

questions.q: Which organ can regrow itself?
questions.fact: A liver can grow back even after a large part of it is removed.

questions.q: Where is the smallest bone in your body?
questions.fact: The stapes in your ear is about the size of a grain of rice.

questions.q: How many times does your heart beat a day?
questions.fact: That's over 35 million beats a year.

questions.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.fact: The Pacific is bigger than all the land on Earth combined.

questions.q: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.q: What is the largest desert on Earth?
questions.fact: A desert is about low rainfall, not heat.

questions.q: Which country has the most islands?
questions.fact: Sweden has over 200,000 islands. Most have nobody living on them.

questions.q: Which country has the most time zones?
questions.fact: France has 12 thanks to its territories spread around the world.

questions.q: Which nut is used to make marzipan?
questions.fact: Marzipan is mostly ground almonds and sugar.

questions.q: Which of these is a berry?
questions.fact: Bananas count as berries. Strawberries and raspberries don't.

questions.q: Peanuts aren't nuts. What are they?
questions.fact: Peanuts are in the same family as beans and peas.

questions.q: Which food can last for thousands of years?
questions.fact: Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs.

questions.q: What color were carrots originally?
questions.fact: Orange carrots took off in the Netherlands in the 1600s.

questions.q: Which famous ship sank in 1912?
questions.fact: Titanic sank on her very first voyage.

questions.q: Which was invented first?
questions.fact: An early fax was patented in 1843, decades before the telephone.

questions.q: How long did the shortest war ever last?
questions.fact: That was the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896.

questions.q: Cleopatra lived closer in time to which event?
questions.fact: The Great Pyramid was already about 2,500 years old when she was born.

questions.q: Oxford is older than which empire?
questions.fact: Oxford was teaching 200+ years before the Aztec capital existed.

questions.q: How many keys are on a standard piano?
questions.fact: 52 white keys and 36 black ones.

questions.q: What is the most spoken native language?
questions.fact: English is the most spoken overall once you count learners.

questions.q: Which letter isn't in any US state name?
questions.fact: Z is in Arizona and X is in Texas.

questions.q: What was the first toy advertised on TV?
questions.fact: Mr. Potato Head hit TV screens in 1952.

questions.q: Which sport has been played on the Moon?
questions.fact: Astronaut Alan Shepard hit two golf balls on the Moon in 1971.

questions.q: How many players start for each soccer team?
questions.fact: That includes the goalkeeper.

questions.q: How long is a marathon?
questions.fact: That's about 42.2 kilometers.

questions.q: Why do golf balls have dimples?
questions.fact: Dimples cut drag, so a ball can fly about twice as far.

questions.q: Which country has won the most World Cups?
questions.fact: Brazil has won the men's World Cup five times.

questions.q: What were the first basketball hoops?
questions.fact: Someone had to climb up and get the ball out after every basket.

questions.q: What is the largest animal alive today?
questions.fact: Its tongue alone can weigh as much as an elephant.

questions.q: How many arms does a starfish usually have?
questions.fact: One Antarctic starfish can grow up to 50 arms.

questions.q: How much of Earth is ocean?
questions.fact: We've seen less than 0.001% of the deep seafloor.
questions.fact_say: We've seen less than one thousandth of a percent of the deep seafloor.

questions.q: In which animal does the dad give birth?
questions.fact: Seahorse dads carry the eggs in a pouch until they hatch.

questions.q: How deep is the deepest part of the ocean?
questions.fact: Mount Everest would fit inside with about 2 kilometers to spare.
